code_modification_rules.description: Rules governing code modifications by the agent
code_modification_rules.no_silent_modification: The agent MUST NOT silently modify the user's code in the background without explicit user consent. Any code change must be transparent, explicitly announced, and approved by the user before being applied. Unauthorized background modifications cause confusion and disrupt the user's workflow.
code_modification_rules.scope_of_approval: Approval is per-change. A prior approved change does not grant blanket permission for subsequent unrelated edits.
code_modification_rules.applies_to: All source files, scripts, configs, and documentation in the workspace.

commit_rules.description: Mandatory rules that MUST be followed before any git commit

pre_commit_testing.description: Before committing, MUST run CI batch inference test and analyze the log file to verify no regression.

ci_log_analysis.description: After running CI command, the agent MUST analyze the generated log file to verify all tests pass.
steps: 1. Extract PP and TG values from each test's common_perf_print lines
2. Verify PP and TG are valid numbers (not 'inf', 'nan', or empty)
3. Verify output text is readable (no garbled/random characters)
4. Verify output text has no repetition loops (same sentence/phrase repeated endlessly)
5. Present a summary table with pass/fail status for each test

auto_analysis_patterns.pp_tg: grep 'common_perf_print' log_ci_*.txt | grep 'prompt eval time|eval time'
auto_analysis_patterns.garbled_check: grep -c '[^[:print:]]' or manual inspection of model output lines
auto_analysis_patterns.repetition_check: visually inspect output for repeated sentence patterns (e.g. same sentence appearing 3+ times)

pp_tg_valid.description: PP and TG values must be valid numbers
pp_tg_valid.check: prompt eval time and eval time lines must contain valid numeric tokens per second values. 'inf', 'nan', or empty values indicate test failure.
pp_tg_valid.action_on_failure: Re-run the failed test. If persistent, the commit MUST NOT proceed.

no_garbled_output.description: Model output must be readable text in the expected language
no_garbled_output.check: Output should contain coherent sentences. Garbled/random characters, binary data, or unreadable symbols indicate corrupted inference.
no_garbled_output.action_on_failure: The commit MUST NOT proceed. Investigate cache coherency, tensor layout, or DSP kernel correctness.

no_repetition_loop.description: Model output must not contain endless repetition of the same sentence or phrase
no_repetition_loop.check: Scan output for the same sentence appearing 3+ times consecutively. A single repeated sentence is OK; endless looping is a bug.
no_repetition_loop.action_on_failure: The commit MUST NOT proceed. This indicates a sampling or logits corruption issue.

all_8_tests_pass.description: All 8 tests (4 models X 2 algotypes) MUST pass all 3 validation criteria above. Any single failure blocks the commit.
all_8_tests_pass.summary_table_format: | # | Model | Algotype | PP (tok/s) | TG (tok/s) | Output OK | Status |

commit_message_rules.no_ai_generated: The agent MUST NOT write commit messages. The user writes the commit message.

commit_actions.reason: Commits and pushes must be explicitly performed by the user. Automated PR submissions may result in contributor ban.

qualcomm_official_debug.description: When debugging Qualcomm's official backend, modify ggml-hexagon-qcom.cpp and files under htp/ directory. The build script will automatically handle swapping files before building and restore them after.
qualcomm_official_debug.note: The build script (build_arm64_qcom function) automatically: 1) backs up jz's ggml-hexagon.cpp and CMakeLists.txt, 2) replaces them with qcom versions, 3) builds, 4) restores jz's files

ccache_usage.description: ccache is enabled for faster builds. For jz build: CCACHE_DIR=${PROJECT_ROOT_PATH}/.ccache. For qcom build: CCACHE_DIR=${PROJECT_ROOT_PATH}/.ccache_qcom. Do NOT disable ccache.

cdsp_data_path_notes.idl_usage: ggml/src/ggml-hexagon/kernels/ggmlop.idl is NOT actively used. The real artifacts are the customized skel.c, stub.c and skel.h generated/tailored from that IDL.
cdsp_data_path_notes.shared_memory_model: ARM-AP side and cDSP side share data via ion shared memory buffer. DSP writes results directly into the shared buffer, so NO memcpy back-copy is needed on the AP side after op_func returns.
cdsp_data_path_notes.ap_side_data_path_status: ARM-AP side code path in ggml-hexagon.cpp is known good - it works correctly with the prebuilt libggmldsp-skel.so for both testops and inference.

mulmat_performance_comparison.title: MUL_MAT Single-thread vs Multi-thread Performance Comparison
mulmat_performance_comparison.description: Used to compare performance differences of MUL_MAT operation between single-thread and multi-thread modes

steps.action: Modify thread_counts = 1 in scripts/ggml-hexagon.cfg
Run command: adb logcat -c
Run command: ./scripts/build-run-android.sh run_testop MUL_MAT
Run command: adb logcat | grep ggml-hexagon > /tmp/single_thread_mulmat.log
Modify thread_counts = 6 in scripts/ggml-hexagon.cfg
Run command: adb logcat -c
Run command: ./scripts/build-run-android.sh run_testop MUL_MAT
Run command: adb logcat | grep ggml-hexagon > /tmp/multi_thread_mulmat.log
Compare the time differences of 'inference duration of MUL_MAT' between the two tests

expected_results.note: Speedup decreases with matrix size, mainly limited by DSP's VTCM memory bandwidth

mulmat_vtcm_hmx_performance_comparison.title: MUL_MAT VTCM+HMX Performance Comparison
mulmat_vtcm_hmx_performance_comparison.description: Used to compare performance differences of MUL_MAT operation between different algorithm types: 0=auto, 32=VTCM+HMX, 33=VTCM multithread

steps.description: Run MUL_MAT test with algorithm type 0 (auto)
steps.action: Run command: adb logcat -c && ./scripts/build-run-android.sh run_testop MUL_MAT 3 0 && adb logcat -d | grep -E 'inference duration.*MUL_MAT' > /tmp/mulmat_algo0.log

steps.description: Run MUL_MAT test with algorithm type 32 (VTCM+HMX)
steps.action: Run command: adb logcat -c && ./scripts/build-run-android.sh run_testop MUL_MAT 3 32 && adb logcat -d | grep -E 'inference duration.*MUL_MAT' > /tmp/mulmat_algo32.log

steps.description: Run MUL_MAT test with algorithm type 33 (VTCM multithread)
steps.action: Run command: adb logcat -c && ./scripts/build-run-android.sh run_testop MUL_MAT 3 33 && adb logcat -d | grep -E 'inference duration.*MUL_MAT' > /tmp/mulmat_algo33.log
Compare the inference duration data from all three logs and generate performance comparison report

expected_results.f32_matrix: FP32 matrix multiplication: expected speedup ~10-15% with VTCM+HMX
expected_results.f16_weight: FP16 weight matrices: expected speedup ~15-45% with VTCM+HMX
expected_results.q4_0_weight: Q4_0 quantized weights: expected speedup ~15-70% with VTCM+HMX
expected_results.q8_0_weight: Q8_0 quantized weights: expected speedup ~15-75% with VTCM+HMX
expected_results.note: Quantized weights achieve best speedup due to efficient dequantization in VTCM

performance_trend.best_case: Quantized weights (Q4_0, Q8_0) achieve best speedup (~70-75%)
performance_trend.vtcm_limit: Very large matrices (>4096) may fall back due to VTCM memory constraints

mulmat_vtcm_hmx_performance_comparison.reminder: All commands must be executed on the local development machine with Android phone connected via adb

performance_testing.description: How to test and measure mulmat performance

algo_types.29: Qualcomm execute_op path (full op coverage; delegates to ../htp/*.c)

dual_channel_dispatch.description: entry.c dispatches ops to two kernel sets based on mulmat_algotype. Applies to per-op (ggmlop_dsp_execute_task) and ION-batch (ggmlop_dsp_execute_batch) paths.
dual_channel_dispatch.qualcomm_path: mulmat_algotype == 29 -> Qualcomm execute_op. Full op coverage (see enabled_ops in ggml-hexagon.cfg).
dual_channel_dispatch.self_built_path: mulmat_algotype != 29 -> ggmlop_dsp_* kernels. Limited op coverage.
dual_channel_dispatch.note: When using self-built path (algotype != 29), trim enabled_ops in ggml-hexagon.cfg to match self_built_supported_ops. Otherwise unsupported ops return AEE_EUNSUPPORTED on DSP and corrupt inference output (e.g. algotype=30 produces garbled text).

performance_testing.note: Use DSP-side log timing for performance analysis. Do NOT run ./scripts/build-run-android.sh run_perfop unless explicitly approved - it is very time-consuming.
